page: Vultr voc-s-16c-128gb-3840s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC processor platform running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz. The configuration allocates 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The memory subsystem provides 128 GB of RAM, yielding an 8 GB per-vCPU ratio. Bundled local storage includes a 3840 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance in stress-ng tests, ranking in the top 25% of comparable cloud hardware with a score of 2912.97. Multi-core compute yields an average classification across synthetic suites, scoring 46204.81 in multi-core stress-ng, 10847.0 in Geekbench multi-core, and 31969.29 in PassMark CPU. Memory bandwidth metrics record uncached read throughput of 123.94 GB/s and write throughput of 70.41 GB/s, while Redis SET operations sustain 28.04 million operations per second and static web throughput reaches 15.37 GB/s.

With a high memory-to-vCPU ratio and high-capacity internal NVMe storage, the configuration provides efficient resource density for persistent input/output and caching workloads without requiring detached network volumes. A key tradeoff is the modest 2.0 GHz clock speed and absence of AVX-512 instruction flags, capping throughput in vector-intensive mathematical routines. The server is well suited for memory-intensive operational databases, large caching clusters, high-capacity file handling, and enterprise web serving stacks.
description: Vultr voc-s-16c-128gb-3840s-amd is an x86_64 Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by a dedicated 16-vCPU, 8-core AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. It features 128 GB of RAM, delivering a memory-dense 8 GB per vCPU, coupled with 3840 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and no GPU hardware. Synthetic testing indicates strong single-core performance alongside average multi-core metrics, achieving 10847.0 in Geekbench multi-core, 31969.29 in PassMark CPU, and 28.04 million Redis operations per second. The combined density of fast local storage and memory capacity makes it cost-efficient for heavy data operations, though constrained in vector computing due to the lack of AVX-512 support. It is technically suited for large relational databases, distributed key-value caches, and static content serving.
